figures.title: Method overview (three-stage pipeline)
figures.panels: Single left-to-right schematic, three stages. Stage 1 Calibration: timeline showing the 120-s calibration prefix disjoint from evaluation windows; EEG+EOG into ridge regression (Eq. 2) + empirical-Bayes shrinkage (Eq. 3) yielding A-tilde_i; small branch showing the reliability criterion routing rejected calibrations to the fallback path (guide withheld). Stage 2 Restoration: evaluation EOG through A-tilde_i forms guide a_i entering the shared U-Net inside the DDIM loop with y and calibration features; Eq. 4 output decomposition drawn as subtraction + two learned corrections. Stage 3 Uncertainty: K trajectories with sampled propagation matrices (Eq. 5) producing a band around the restored waveform. Color code: blue = shared population components, orange = calibration-derived quantities, gray = fallback. All illustrative waveform snippets (EOG drive, contaminated, restored mean, 80% band) rendered from the real exemplar arrays in t6_waveform_exemplar_dev.npz (keys eog_drive, contaminated, matched, band_mean, band_halfwidth_80, channel Fp1) — no synthetic waveforms, no performance numbers in the diagram.
figures.claim: The system calibrates a propagation matrix from a separate 120-s segment, guides a shared diffusion model with propagated EOG, withholds the guide when calibration fails the reliability criterion, and reports intervals that include propagation uncertainty.
figures.honesty_note: Diagram only — no measured values may appear; the fallback (refusal) path must be drawn as a first-class branch, not omitted.

figures.title: DS-DDPM reproduction findings
figures.section: Sec 5.7 Benchmark/reproduction context — NEW figure (currently text-only)
figures.panels: Panel A: grand-mean summary dot plot across all 12 protocol variants (3 arms {raw, ica, dsddpm} x 4 recipes {paper, adam, adam_l2, adam_zscore}) from results/paper_final/dsddpm/table1_{raw,ica,dsddpm}[_adam|_adam_l2|_adam_zscore].json — all cluster at 0.25-0.28 vs the published references (ICA M-mean 50.58%, DS-DDPM 52.87%) drawn as reference lines, chance 0.25 marked, with EEGNet-8,2 within-participant 66% as a third tick showing the data supports learning; inset: one representative 9x9 accuracy matrix trio (table1_raw.json, table1_ica.json, table1_dsddpm_paper.json). Panel B: side-by-side 9x9 heatmaps real_real vs gen_real PSD-signature correlations from table2_correlations.json — real_real off-diagonal ~0.94 with subject 6 ~0.68 vs gen_real flat everywhere (diag mean 0.3917 vs off-diag 0.3929: generated subject noise carries no subject identity). Panel C: training-loss curves (total + time_diff, noise_kl, sub_arc, orth components; 8100 steps = 100 epochs x 81 steps) from results/paper_final/dsddpm/train_metrics.csv — total 3.38 -> 0.69, sub_arc -> 1.2e-4, i.e. training converged, ruling out an under-training explanation.
figures.claim: Under twelve frozen protocol variants the DS-DDPM cross-subject backbone sits at chance (0.25-0.28 vs published 50.6/52.9%) while EEGNet reaches 66% on the same data, and its generated subject noise shows no subject specificity (matched 0.392 vs mismatched 0.393) — reported factually as a reproduction finding.
figures.honesty_note: Caveats stated in caption: the release has no denoise-recorded-EEG path (both samplers start from Gaussian noise), the classifier is unreleased, the Table II computation is unreleased, and the PSD-signature choice was frozen before numbers were seen. This is a reproduction report, not an attack; the converged-training panel exists precisely to rule out the cheap explanation.

verdict.problems: Panel A names "EEGNet-8,2 within-participant 66%" but no listed data_file (and no file found anywhere on disk) contains that number; the only machine-readable within-participant EEGNet-8,2 result on BCI-IV-2a is results/paper_final/bci2a/route1.json RAW arm = 0.593 mean (per-subject 0.389-0.830, official T->E split), contradicting 66% (which exists only as prose "~66%" in RESULTS_PAPER_FINAL.md line 365). Two minor issues: (1) train_metrics.csv is headerless (8100 rows x 6 unnamed columns); component identities are recoverable only from the writer at scripts/paper_final/dsddpm_repro.py (order: total, total-orth-sub_arc, time_diff, noise_kl, sub_arc, orth) - verified numerically (col0 3.384->0.687, sub_arc->1.23e-4). (2) Panel B caption "real_real off-diagonal ~0.94" is only true excluding subject 6; the overall off-diagonal mean is 0.887. Everything else verified: all 14 files exist; 12 grand_means span 0.2524-0.2767; published_reference 50.58/52.87 present; 9x9 matrices present; gen_real diag 0.3917 vs off-diag 0.3929; subject-6 off-diag 0.686.
verdict.fix: Repair the 66% tick: either (a) source it from results/paper_final/bci2a/route1.json RAW arm and relabel it "EEGNet-8,2 within-participant, official T->E: 59.3% (mean, n=9)" - which still makes the data-supports-learning point - and add route1.json to data_files; or (b) drop the tick and state the point in the caption citing route1.json. Do not print 66% (no on-disk source; contradicted by route1.json). For Panel C, hardcode the CSV column mapping [total, base, time_diff, noise_kl, sub_arc, orth] with a comment pointing to scripts/paper_final/dsddpm_repro.py's writerow. For Panel B, phrase the caption as "off-diagonal 0.887 overall (0.944 excluding subject 6, whose off-diagonal is ~0.69)". With these repairs the figure is fully buildable from files on disk.

figures.title: Single-channel benchmark across SNR
figures.section: Sec 5.7 Benchmark context — per-SNR companion to the benchmark table
figures.panels: 2x2 or 2x3 line-panel grid: rows = {EOG, EMG}, columns = {CC, RRMSE_t} (optionally RRMSE_s), 11 SNR levels -5..+5 dB, one line per arm (Noisy, SDEdit, CondDiff, FCNN, SimpleCNN, ComplexCNN, RNN_LSTM, NovelCNN) from results/paper_final/e12/EOG_grid.csv and EMG_grid.csv (per-SNR rows; overall rows excluded from the lines and quoted in the caption: EOG SimpleCNN CC 0.9336 vs CondDiff 0.8880; EMG NovelCNN 0.8775 vs CondDiff 0.7625; SDEdit below Noisy on EOG).
figures.claim: Our noisy-conditioned diffusion is competitive on the EEGdenoiseNet grid (beats the unconditional prior and 2/5 supervised baselines) but does not beat the best supervised CNNs — context, not a contest.
figures.honesty_note: SDEdit underperforms even the Noisy input on EOG (CC 0.6083 vs 0.6691) and CondDiff loses to SimpleCNN/NovelCNN — all eight lines plotted, none dropped, per the no-overclaiming discipline.

verdict.fix: No repair needed for the panels — both CSVs contain all 8 methods x 11 SNR levels x {cc, rrmse_t, rrmse_s} plus overall rows, and every caption number matches exactly. One caption-wording precision: scope "beats 2/5 supervised baselines" to EOG (CC: CondDiff 0.8880 > FCNN 0.8771 and RNN_LSTM 0.8238); on EMG CondDiff (CC 0.7625) beats 0/5 supervised arms, though it does beat SDEdit and Noisy on both artifacts.

figures.title: Interval width localization
figures.section: Sec 5.4 / Appendix — mechanism detail for the interval claims (currently unfigured)
figures.panels: Single scatter, 270 cells from t6_width_locality.npz: propagation width share Var_op/(sigma^2+Var_op) (y; 0-0.519, mean 0.30) vs calibration within-variance within_v (x, log scale; 7.6e-5 to 64.1), points colored by EB shrinkage lambda (lam, 0-0.9999) with hard_gate=1 cells (4.4%) marked by a distinct outline; marginal histogram of width share showing the ~0.30 operator contribution.
figures.claim: Interval width localizes to unreliable calibrations: the operator-propagation term contributes a roughly ~0.30 mean share of squared width and grows with calibration within-variance, and gated cells sit where the shrinkage/reliability machinery says they should.
figures.honesty_note: Supports the mechanism narrative only; the dev temperature ranges (2.30-2.55 vs 2.90-3.20) quoted alongside it in the text have no banked sweep data and stay text-only.
